svg.title: Proof. Each actual conclusive branch is precisely η times its ideal branch on every ρSR by Eq. (29). The conclusive difference is negative with total trace 1 −η. The orthogonal actual null block is positive with the same trace. Adding the block trace norms gives 2(1 −η). The same argument survives classical charge recording, since the conclusive factorization and null trace remain exact. This is an exact full-output identity, not a scalar probability bound substituted for an instrument error. □ The isometry P y Fy ⊗|y⟩with a neutral outcome pointer commutes with total charge and extends to a blockwise charge-preserving unitary. The coherent charge-copy map has the same property. Hence the model has a finite unitary realization; it has not hidden a noninvariant Fourier gate in the apparatus. A common fixed readout of the outcome pointer supplies the declared instrument. Reading additional microscopic pointer/environment degrees of freedom requires declaring their common states and couplings as well; no universal detector equivalence follows. The finite resource ledger of this explicit dilation is: source dimension N, active reference dimension M, neutral charge-archive dimension N + M −1, and neutral outcome-pointer dimension N + 1, plus the nominated fixed controller/clock and arbitrary inert R. A coherent charge archive is quantum memory; a classical one still retains its entire record. The optimum in Eq. (24) counts populated phase-reference charge sectors only. It is not a bound on total apparatus or complete-archive dimension, and it does not identify a single-use Choi rank with retained history capacity.
